items.title: Sotheby's Maison Presents Major Yayoi Kusama Career Retrospective Exhibition
items.text: Sotheby's Maison Presents Major Yayoi Kusama Career Retrospective Exhibition Summary Sotheby's Salon in Hong Kong presents a major exhibition celebrating the seven-decade career of artist Yayoi KusamaThe curated showcase features rare works spanning the 1950s to 2010s across three thematic sectionsThe exhibition is currently open at Sotheby's Maison through August 20, 2026 Sotheby’s Salon has officially opened a major exhibition celebrating legendary Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama at 1/F, Sotheby’s Maison in Hong Kong's The Landmark. Tracing seven decades of influential output, the retrospective highlights paintings, works on paper, and screenprints spanning from the 1950s to the 2010s.Organized into three distinct thematic sections—Nature and Nurture, Fauna and Flora, and The Urban and Pop—the exhibition charts Kusama's artistic evolution from her formative years in Japan through her groundbreaking period in the United States and her return home. Key early highlights include The Pacific Ocean No. A.B.X. (1959), a rare ink, pastel, and gouache work executed shortly after her arrival in New York.The showcase also features canvas pieces such as Sunset Grapes (1988), which transforms organic forms into vibrant patterns of repetition, and the rarely seen Handbag (1984), demonstrating her engagement with consumer culture, fashion, and everyday objects. Together with examples of her celebrated Infinity Nets, pumpkins, and floral imagery, the selection offers a comprehensive view of the artist's enduring visual universe.The Yayoi Kusama exhibition is currently open to the public at 1/F, Sotheby’s Maison, running through August 20, 2026.Sotheby's Maison1/F, LANDMARK CHATER8 Connaught Road CentralCentral, Hong Kong Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: PARCO Unveils Its 2026 Fall/Winter Campaign, "NOSTALGIC FUTURE"
items.text: PARCO Unveils Its 2026 Fall/Winter Campaign, "NOSTALGIC FUTURE" PARCO, which not only operates fashion buildings in Japan but also promotes cutting-edge culture through venues such as theaters, cinemas, and live music halls, has unveiled its advertising campaign for the Fall/Winter 2026 season built around the concept of "NOSTALGIC FUTURE."Serving as creative director is Christophe Brunnquell, one of Europe's foremost creatives, who spent 15 years as the founding art director of Purple, the storied independent French fashion magazine. At the heart of the "NOSTALGIC FUTURE" concept is LE COEUR JAPONAIS (The Japanese Heart), a book published in 1927 by Brunnquell's great-grandfather, the philosopher and writer Félicien Challaye. Written after Challaye's travels through Japan, the book reflects his fascination with the spirituality and virtues of the Japanese people. Its enduring portrait of the Japanese spirit, along with its ideas connecting West and East, memory and future, forms the creative foundation of this campaign nearly a hundred years later.The campaign is set within a Western-style mansion on the outskirts of Paris. Casting both Eastern and Western models, and framing them amid scattered books, sculptures that carry a sense of history, and antique furniture, the visuals fuse elements drawn from the past with staging that looks toward the future, constructing a world that belongs to no single era. The result is imagery in which distinct timelines appear to intersect within a single frame. Equally striking is the way the passage of time is expressed through color, shifting from autumnal looks centered on ecru and navy toward winter looks defined by deep reds and magentas.Speaking about the project, Brunnquell commented, "I believe the future is always built from memories, traditions, and stories that existed before us." He described nostalgia not as a simple act of looking back, but as "a creative force for imagining the future," explaining that he built the campaign by weaving together his own roots and his respect for Japanese culture.Taking a single book written nearly 100 years ago as its point of departure, PARCO's 2026 Fall/Winter campaign, "NOSTALGIC FUTURE," presents a worldview that moves fluidly across past and future, West and East. Additional videos and visuals are available on the special campaign website and PARCO's official YouTube channel. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: LinkedIn Introduces New "Seems Like AI Slop" Reporting Button to Combat Feed Spam
items.text: LinkedIn Introduces New "Seems Like AI Slop" Reporting Button to Combat Feed Spam Summary LinkedIn launched a user reporting tool that allows members to flag feed content as "Seems like AI slop" to combat machine-generated spam.The platform is officially retiring its AI-driven post enhancement feature and introducing a proofreading tool that preserves the original author's voice.New backend classifiers and profile verification rollouts aim to clean up the professional network after reports showed massive spikes in automated posts. LinkedIn is officially pushing back against the flood of machine-generated feed spam. The professional networking platform rolled out a new reporting button that allows users to flag content specifically as "Seems like AI slop." Tucked inside the standard three-dot menu on any post, the tool lets human readers police the timeline. The move marks a direct response to a growing cultural frustration with synthetic engagement bait that has increasingly dominated the site.Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan announced the measures directly, noting that authentic human connection remains the core focus for the company. To support the user-facing reporting button, LinkedIn is ramping up backend classifiers designed to detect low-quality automation before it hits the feed. The system is already working overtime. According to Srinivasan, the platform currently blocks hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts daily and has thwarted billions of broad automation actions over the past few months alone.The company is also walking back some of its own previous AI integrations. LinkedIn is removing a tool that offered to "enhance" user posts with artificial intelligence. In its place, the platform will introduce a standard proofreading feature built to check spelling and grammar while preserving the original voice of the author. For creators, the backend analytics dashboard will soon test a private flagging system. If multiple users report a specific post as inauthentic or heavily reliant on AI, the original author will receive a quiet notification.The anti-slop campaign arrives just as third-party data paints a stark picture of the network's current state. A recent study by AI detection firm Pangram revealed that 41 percent of long-form posts on LinkedIn registered as completely machine-written. items.title: Electronic Arts Set to Finalize $55 Billion USD Go-Private Acquisition
items.text: Electronic Arts Set to Finalize $55 Billion USD Go-Private Acquisition Summary Electronic Arts has confirmed that all regulatory approvals for its $55 billion merger have been securedThe record-breaking buyout is led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity PartnersUpon closing on August 4, EA will delist from Nasdaq while retaining Andrew Wilson as CEO and remaining in Redwood City Electronic Arts is set to officially close its record-breaking $55 billion USD go-private deal after securing all necessary regulatory approvals. The video game publisher expects the transaction to finalize on or about the close of trading on August 4, 2026.The historic buyout is spearheaded by a consortium comprising Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, with stockholders receiving $210 USD per share in cash. Once completed, the publisher behind major franchises such as Battlefield 6, The Sims, and Madden NFL will delist from the NASDAQ and transition into a privately held company.Despite the shift in corporate ownership, EA will remain headquartered in Redwood City, California, with Andrew Wilson continuing his role as CEO to oversee operations across its global studio network.The $55 billion USD merger is expected to officially close on August 4, 2026. items.title: Le Labo Dedicates “SHIU 25” City Exclusive Scent to Beijing’s Sacred Courtyards
items.text: Le Labo Dedicates “SHIU 25” City Exclusive Scent to Beijing’s Sacred Courtyards Summary Le Labo's SHIU 25 anchors powdery iris, olibanum and warm woods around the serene, balancing Shiu note.The scent draws inspiration from Beijing's He Yuan Lab, a restored Siheyuan courtyard blending wabi-sabi aesthetics with ancient heritage.Available exclusively in Beijing year-round, it'll be available globally for a limited time. Le Labo expands its coveted City Exclusive Collection with SHIU 25, an Eau de Parfum dedicated to the city of Beijing. Conceived as an homage to traditional spaces built for quietude and inner return, the fragrance captures the soul of the house's historic Beijing He Yuan Lab — a culturally protected Siheyuan courtyard nestled in House 19 at Wang Fu Central.Global Brand President and Creative Director Deborah Royer describes the creation as "an invitation to find centered calm, self-reflection, and a moment of pause in a world that rarely grants one". By weaving the spirit of ancient craftsmanship with modern contemplation, SHIU 25 serves as an olfactory refuge where creation flows effortlessly from stillness.The scent narrative centers on Shiu, the quieter and more serene expression of the Ho tree, long revered for its ability to bring balance and inner peace. In this intentionally compact composition, ethereal notes of powdery iris and sacred olibanum float weightlessly above a grounding foundation of warm, anchoring woods. The experience unfolds like a serene walk through hidden courtyard gardens, where gentle shadows dance across well-worn wooden floors and the creative spirit awakens in sacred silence. Soft, resinous, and deeply comforting, SHIU 25 wraps the wearer in an enveloping atmosphere of centered calm, offering a quiet return to the timeless wisdom of the senses.In true Le Labo fashion, the fragrance is presented in the brand's iconic industrial-apothecary glass bottle, topped with a minimalist metallic cap and finished with a personalized, typewriter-style label detailing the scent name, date, and owner's name. For display, the collection is housed in raw, crate-like wooden packaging that reflects the house's signature wabi-sabi aesthetic, bridging utilitarian design with unpretentious luxury. While SHIU 25 resides exclusively year-round at the Beijing He Yuan Lab, it travels worldwide for Le Labo's annual City Exclusive event. items.title: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' Understands Exactly What It Needs to Be
items.text: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' Understands Exactly What It Needs to Be The world didn't necessarily need a sequel to The Devil Wears Prada. It’s not a criticism, just a fact about revisiting a movie that ended exactly where it needed to. And yet, 20 years later, David Frankel and writer Aline Brosh McKenna have uncovered a narrative premise that actually justifies reopening the doors of Runway: a media industry collapsing under its own weight and the people who build their careers in the twilight of its golden years refusing to be quietly consumed by it.The Devil Wears Prada 2's setup alone handles so much heavy lifting. Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway) the award-winning investigative journalist, loses her job with a text — the universe’s passive-aggressive, late-stage-capitalist answer to a final dismissal. Miranda Priestly (Meryl Streep) finds herself scrambling to adapt to a digitally focused media landscape and staring down a forced retirement. Emily Charlton (Emily Blunt), Miranda's former first assistant who approaches the idea of a trip to Paris as if she were commanding troops, reinvents herself as a powerhouse Dior executive who has the kind of revenue Miranda is suddenly dependent upon. And if this power triangle sounds uncannily familiar to any recent media professional, then good, you’ve been paying attention. That is the core insight this film has: what’s the worst thing about media becoming a wasteland? It's not the layoffs or the ever-shrinking masthead. It’s seeing everyone who cemented this status quo utterly bested.The magic is the script does not force a sentimental decline of Miranda. Streep plays her as someone the last 20 years have merely honed, who has ceded her ego’s more monstrous impulses for an amplified sense of conviction. It’s such a subtle, believable transformation, and only a transformation as nuanced as this one would have held. The fashion is, as it should be, something to talk about on its own. Costume designer Molly Rogers (who also worked on the Sex and the City spinoff ...And Just Like That) steps in to replace legendary Patricia Field, creating thought selections with deliberate intentionality. Miranda's weathered Dries Van Noten toreador jacket, trimmed with the perfect turquoise, is a prime example of the garment’s ability to reward a deeper view. items.title: Billie Eilish's "Eilish Intense" Eau de Parfum Deepens Its Amber Gourmand Into a Nighttime Signature
items.text: Billie Eilish's "Eilish Intense" Eau de Parfum Deepens Its Amber Gourmand Into a Nighttime Signature Summary Eilish Intense amplifies the original Eilish Eau de Parfum with a richer, more enveloping take on its amber gourmand profileThe composition moves from red berries and mandarin through creamy vanilla and cocoa into a dry down of warm musks, tonka bean, and woodsThe collection's sculptural bust-inspired bottle is reimagined in a luminous radiant gold to mirror the scent's intensified warmth Eilish Fragrances has unveiled Eilish Intense, a deeper evolution of Billie Eilish's award-winning debut scent developed in partnership with Parlux. Rather than reinvent the formula, Intense amplifies the warmth and sensuality of the original amber gourmand, reworking its structure into a fuller, more enveloping expression built for after-dark wear.The composition opens on a luminous contrast of red berries and mandarin, wrapped in what the brand describes as the textural sweetness of sugared petals. From there it moves into a heart of creamy vanilla, soft spices, and cocoa, the trio responsible for the addictive richness that defines the scent's middle stretch. The dry down is where Intense earns its name, settling into warm musks, tonka bean, and sleek woods that linger against the skin. It is a recognizable extension of the original's creamy vanilla signature, tuned for depth rather than novelty, and Eilish herself has framed the split plainly: the original for daytime, Intense for night.The bottle carries the concept in physical form. Eilish Intense retains the collection's sculptural silhouette, an abstract interpretation of the human bust, now finished in a luminous radiant gold chosen to reflect the fragrance's intensified warmth. The design leans on Eilish's stated view of fragrance bottles as standalone objects, and the outer carton extends the treatment with gold and iridescent detailing that reinforces the collection's richer visual world.The sustainability credentials remain consistent with the rest of the line. Eilish Intense is vegan, paraben-free, and formulated with clean ingredients, while the carton is printed with Envirofoil and produced using 100 percent renewable wind energy. The fragrance is also PETA-certified cruelty-free through the organization's Global Beauty Without Bunnies program, keeping the flanker aligned with the brand's established formulation and packaging standards.Eilish Intense is available now online, with the full collection

items.title: The 2027 Met Gala Will Be All About John Galliano
items.text: The 2027 Met Gala Will Be All About John Galliano Summary The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced that John Galliano will be the subject of its spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibitionTitled John Galliano Horizons the exhibition marks the first major museum retrospective examining the full breadth of his four-decade careerThe show will be on view at The Met Fifth Avenue from May 9 2027 through January 9 2028 The Metropolitan Museum of Art has officially announced that John Galliano will be the subject of its landmark Spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition as well as the Met Gala, titled John Galliano: Horizons. Galliano becomes only the third living designer in history to receive a solo exhibition at The Met, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017.Curated by Andrew Bolton, Curator in Charge of The Costume Institute, the retrospective spans Galliano’s career from his 1984 Central Saint Martins graduation collection through his celebrated tenures at Givenchy, Christian Dior, and Maison Margiela. Drawing heavily from The Costume Institute’s extensive archives, the exhibition features garments, accessories, sketches, research books, toiles, and culminates with his Spring/Summer 2024 Maison Margiela Artisanal presentation.The curation is organized into three distinct thematic sections: "Bearings," "Horizons," and "Atlas of Transformation." In addition to showcasing his technical mastery and artistic vision, the opening section "Bearings" will directly examine his 2010 and 2011 conduct, his dismissal from Dior, and the ongoing cultural dialogue surrounding accountability and legacy.John Galliano: Horizons will serve as the centerpiece for the 2027 Met Gala and will be open to the public at The Met Fifth Avenue from May 9, 2027 through January 9, 2028. items.text: Travis Scott Drops 'Odyssey' Merch & SS27 Trends Heat up in This Week's Top Fashion News  Summary SS27 menswear focused on heat-beating sheer fabrics and vibrant hues. SATISFY and Levi's delivered climbing-ready denim, while McDonald's China dropped a functional paper-bag backpack.Travis Scott merged cinematic merch with IMAX, and NikeSKIMS leveled up its sculpting wear.The SS27 Trends: What Comes After Fashion's Hottest Season Ever? As European summers grew more brutal, the Spring/Summer 2027 menswear collections offered a refreshing cooldown. Paris and Milan runways ditched the heavy tailoring of seasons past for fluid, joy-driven ensembles built to beat the heat. Designers championed sheer shirting reminiscent of the traditional Filipino barong, which let the breeze flow through ultra-lightweight, transparent constructions. Silky satins elevated everyday shirting and trousers into billowing, breathable statements, while shrunken “micro jackets” shed unnecessary bulk. The color palettes shifted dramatically too, and leaned heavily into aquatic blues and sunset-inspired oranges to capture the essence of seaside escapes. Completing the relaxed resort vibe, the boxer short fully cemented itself as the ultimate bottom of the season, which prioritized ultimate freedom and ventilation.Cactus Jack Launches Exclusive Clothing Capsule for 'The Odyssey' and IMAX Travis Scott celebrated his self-directed short film for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey and dropped a highly limited Cactus Jack capsule. The collection debuted alongside the film's premiere and his featured end-credits track, "When I'm Home," merging cinematic aesthetics with Scott’s signature graphic-heavy streetwear. The limited drop was available for just one week and featured co-branded T-shirts, a long-sleeve, and a tote bag emblazoned with official IMAX insignia. Retail prices ranged comfortably from $55 to $75 USD. While the public release strictly focused on apparel, the collaboration also yielded two cast-and-crew exclusive footwear models—the Nike Moon Shoe and the ACG Moc—which proved Scott’s continued ability to fuse blockbuster narrative storytelling with highly sought-after product design.SATISFY Reconnects With Levi's for a Second Climbing-Focused Capsule Parisian running label SATISFY and American denim brand Levi’s joined forces once again for a specialized, climbing-centric capsule. items.title: Precious Okoyomon Unveils 25-Foot Teddy Bear Slide at MoMA PS1
items.text: Precious Okoyomon Unveils 25-Foot Teddy Bear Slide at MoMA PS1 Summary Artist Precious Okoyomon has unveiled an outdoor installation at New York's MoMA PS1The artwork features a wild garden, sound installations, and a giant teddy bear sculptureThe installation, the inaugural Courtyard Commission, will be on view for two years. For the next two years, the courtyard at MoMA PS1 will play host to Precious Okoyomon’s playground of pleasures. The New York-based artist, known for their lush gardenscapes and cute-creepy stuffed animal sculptures, has planted a living forest in even in the balmiest of New York heat for “Among the Flowers I Learned to Love: A Garden of Decreation,” their largest outdoor piece yet.Taking place on a plush bed of 1,500 perennials and plants, the installation is a sensorial blend of blooms, sculpture, and sound, co-cultivated with Rhode Island nursery issima. Oppositional species — native and invasive plants — grow beside one another, with pollinators and butterflies abound, creating a scene that challenges ideas of what can cultivate together.Okoyomon’s garden envisions life eternally in flux, inspired by philosopher Simone Weil’s concept of "decreation" — the constant making and unmaking of the world. As plants shift, seasons change, the space hones in on environmental and social realities of adaptation, resilience, and the unpredictable future of urban nature in shifting climates. View this post on InstagramA post shared by HypeArt (@hypeart)At the heart of the installation is “The Pleasure Principle,” a 25-foot-long sculpture. Visitors can climb into a teddy bear and listen to Okoyomon reading their poetry as they ride down a blood-red slide before exiting through its mouth. The adorable character is a recurring motif for the artist, often tied to idea(l)s of pleasure, while embodying the space between inner and outer worlds, à la Winnicott.“Among the Flowers I Learned to Love: A Garden of Decreation” (2026) is now on view for free in New York, and marks the inaugural piece of the museum’s experimental Courtyard Commissions series. Check out PS1’s website for more details.MoMA PS122-25 Jackson Ave,Queens, NY 11101 Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: Why the Best Part of Golf Happens Before the First Tee The best rounds begin long before anyone pulls a club out of the bag. From deciding the day's format to debating handicaps and playlists on the drive over, the moments leading up to a round have become just as much a part of the experience as the golf itself. Created in partnership with the All-New 2026 Toyota RAV4, Hypegolf's latest campaign explores that idea through The Game Before the Game, celebrating the rituals, conversations and camaraderie that define a day on the course. At the heart of the story is the drive itself, where the All-New 2026 Toyota RAV4 becomes the starting point for a day built around golf, friendship and time spent outdoors.At the center of the story is professional skateboarder, podcast host and Golf With Flavor founder Justin Eldridge, who assembled his ideal foursome for a day of golf in Los Angeles. Joined by his wife Ali Eldridge, skateboarding legend Jose Rojo and snowboarding pioneer Russell Winfield, the group heads to the course together in the Toyota RAV4 before settling into a day built around friendship as much as competition. Alongside the campaign film and accompanying lookbook, Eldridge reflects on the connection between skateboarding and golf, the value of community and why the drive to the course is often where the day really begins.Hypegolf: For people who know you from skateboarding, how did golf become part of your life?Justin Eldridge: I actually got hurt and wasn't able to skate for a few months. A friend and I decided to go to the driving range, and the place had a par-3 course that stayed lit up until 10PM. It was the perfect combination, and I was hooked from the start.You've built communities in both skateboarding and golf. What similarities do you see between those two worlds?There are so many similarities, it's crazy. From the camaraderie and friendships that are built to the style and the way everybody just wants each other to win and have fun, the overlap is huge. To me, golf courses are just big skate parks.For this project, you brought together your own foursome. What made this the right group of people to spend the day with?I think that being able to spend the day with people you have fun with and respect is a huge part of the game. items.title: How Oakley’s 'Future Genesis' Characters Mirror Its Endless Drive For Innovation
items.text: How Oakley’s 'Future Genesis' Characters Mirror Its Endless Drive For Innovation View this post on InstagramA post shared by HYPEBEAST (@hypebeast) For nearly half a century, Oakley’s brand identity has been anchored by its persistent refusal to conform to standard industry norms, preferring to actively build the future rather than remaining passive for its arrival. Through the expansion of its narrative universe in Future Genesis, Oakley translates this distinct design philosophy into a sci-fi story. The characters traversing this storm-ravaged world are personifications of the exact mindset that has fueled the brand for decades which means never settling, always progressing, and always looking toward what’s next.The narrative's evolution finds Max Fearlight, a brilliant inventor whose relentless drive to solve problems reflects Oakley’s foundational commitment to engineering solutions from scratch. Max refuses to live under the strict, mind-purifying mandates of authoritarian cities like CIV17, declaring in his journal entries that "a human with such strict limitations cannot evolve" and that "if we are to find a way to navigate the challenges we face, we must do so without fear". His personality is defined by technical precision and protective determination. When faced with lethal thermonuclear storms, Max doesn't surrender to despair; he retrofits an abandoned water purification facility into an advanced self-sustaining bunker, engineering Iridium-infused lenses, wind generators, and closed-loop survival systems. His relentless pursuit of technological mastery mirrors Oakley’s own obsession with pushing the boundaries of material science and functional design.However, while Max focuses on building physical and digital shields—evidenced by his obsession with creating the "Echoverse" to keep his family secure—his daughter, Maxine, represents the next evolutionary step of that same progressive ethos. Maxine possesses a fierce, boundary-pushing curiosity that prevents her from settling for comfortable isolation. While her father views the outside world as a closed door, Maxine looks beyond the bunker walls with an unyielding longing for discovery. As a child, when Max warns her of the severe atmospheric hazards outside, Maxine’s instinct is not to retreat, but to push forward, boldly telling her mother that "all we're building is a prison" when arguing against complete shelter containment. items.text: DSM Kei Ninomiya Spotlights a Diverse Cast of Creatives for Its FW26 Campaign Summary DSM's Kei Ninomiya FW26 campaign features a diverse cast of international creatives Hiroshi Fujiwara, Hirokazu Kore-eda and more.The collection concept subverts football apparel, reworking sportswear into cultural expression.Available now across DSM flagships and online platforms. Dover Street Market and Kei Ninomiya have teamed up for a striking Fall/Winter 2026 campaign that highlights a diverse ensemble cast of international creatives. The campaign brings together artists, musicians, models and tastemakers from varied disciplines, spanning figures such as Hiroshi Fujiwara, acclaimed filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda, actress Miwako Ichikawa, costume designer Michiko Kitamura to Avu-Chan - the lead singer of alternative Japanese band Queen Bee - and more.At the core of the collection's concept is the subversion of football apparel, taking sports-derived garments beyond their traditional field settings and expanding them into a broader cultural language. By stripping these athletic motifs of their original context, the lineup transforms a strictly codified sport into a medium for free thinking and uninhibited expression. Designed as "clothes for nameless communities," the pieces break down the rigid boundaries of defined fanbases or subcultures, thus bending the rules within a sportswear framework.The DSM Kei Ninomiya FW26 range is now available across the retailers' flagships and online shops. View this post on Instagram A post shared by DSM Kei Ninomiya (@dsmkeininomiya) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: A First Look at Nike and Zellerfeld’s 3D-Printed Air Works Prototype Name: Motoi Hatsuki Air Works 3D-printed SneakerSKU: TBCRelease Date: TBCNike has officially taken its first public step into the future of footwear manufacturing with its 3D-printed sneaker from its innovative Air Works Program, developed in partnership with additive manufacturing specialist Zellerfeld.Revealed via social media by Blue Room's Motoi Hatsuki, the prototype silhouette showcases a sleek, monochromatic model. The sneaker features a one‑piece 3D‑printed construction, eliminating traditional stitching and overlays for a streamlined, slip‑on profile. Hatsuki’s design draws inspiration from the Air Max 1000 and Tailwind V, incorporating exaggerated heel and forefoot Air bubbles, including a glowing neon yellow unit at the rear. The side panels showcase a paisley‑style looping motif, adding ornamental depth to the otherwise minimal structure. Branding is kept subtle, allowing the experimental form and texture to take center stage.As part of Nike’s broader Air Works initiative, which brought eight global creatives to Beaverton to collaborate with Nike engineers. Each participant will receive limited friends‑and‑family runs of their concepts, with previews rolling out ahead of Air Max Day 2027. View this post on Instagram A post shared by htk (@htk2626) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: The STEKA Octagonal Aluminum Pan Is Built for a Lifetime of Fire and Flame
items.text: The STEKA Octagonal Aluminum Pan Is Built for a Lifetime of Fire and Flame Summary ADDI designs the STEKA, an octagonal sauté pan for Mozambique, blending Scandinavian minimalism with Japanese craftsmanship.Features include a solid aluminum body, a removable handle and a drop-lid-inspired cover.Available now via Mozambique’s webstore, priced at around $172 USD. STEKA is an octagonal aluminum sauté pan designed by Swedish studio ADDI for Japanese cookware brand Mozambique. Conceived as a versatile cooking tool that bridges indoor kitchens and rugged outdoor environments, the pan was designed from a philosophy of structural logic and reduction rather than fleeting trends. Intended to transition seamlessly from a standard kitchen stove to an open campfire, the STEKA pan is engineered to be an adaptable, lifelong culinary instrument that ages and develops character alongside its owner.Crafted from 5 mm solid aluminum, STEKA offers heat retention similar to cast iron but with a lighter weight. Its high, straight sides expand cooking possibilities, while the removable cast‑aluminum handle, secured with a single stainless‑steel screw, allows for easy replacement, oven use, or compact storage. The companion lid, inspired by the Japanese otoshibuta drop‑lid, features raised points underneath that circulate moisture during simmering and braising, creating a self‑basting effect. Each piece is hand‑finished, with production limited to ten units per day, underscoring its artisanal quality.Available now via Mozambique's webstore, the STEKA pan retails at ¥27,500 JPY (approx. $172 USD) and comes with a five‑year warranty. items.title: Pharrell Williams’ JOOPITER Launches Its First-Ever Dedicated Watch Auction
items.text: Pharrell Williams’ JOOPITER Launches Its First-Ever Dedicated Watch Auction Summary JOOPITER debuts Keeping Measure: Watches & Timepieces, its first watch auction.Features collectible pieces from Patek Philippe, OMEGA, Cartier and more.Bidding is open until August 5, 2026, with highlights like the Alan Bean Speedmaster and HYT Moon Runner Red Magma. JOOPITER has announced its first auction under its newly established Watches Department, titled Keeping Measure: Watches & Timepieces. Curated to showcase both landmark models from storied Maisons and innovative creations from independent watchmakers, the sale spans over half a century of horological design. Featuring names such as Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, OMEGA, Piaget, Cartier, Ressence, HYT, Speake‑Marin and Ōtsuka Lotēc, the auction reflects the breadth of contemporary collecting and aims to appeal to seasoned collectors as well as newcomers.The auction is currently open for bidding until August 5, 2026, with highlights including rare OMEGA pieces such as a tropical dial 2915‑3 and the first auction appearance of the complicated Speedmaster Chrono Chime. Other standout lots include the OMEGA Alan Bean Speedmaster produced in 1969 and linked to the astronaut who became the fourth person to walk on the Moon; the Ulysse Nardin 18k Woven Bracelet Watch crafted by Gay Frères; as well as the HYT Moon Runner Red Magma -- a bold 2022 release showcasing HYT’s liquid‑time technology. Head over to JOOPITER's dedicated webpage to view the full lineup of the Keeping Measure: Watches & Timepieces sale. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: David Zwirner Announces a Two-Location Yoshitomo Nara Showcase in NYC
items.text: David Zwirner Announces a Two-Location Yoshitomo Nara Showcase in NYC Summary Yoshitomo Nara’s first David Zwirner exhibition opens in New York on October 29, 2026.The two-location exhibition features new atmospheric paintings and large-format drawings.The 19th Street location will feature thirteen monumental white bronze head sculptures. Opening this fall, David Zwirner will present Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara’s inaugural solo exhibition with the gallery, spanning its 533 West 19th Street and 537 West 20th Street locations in New York. Marking the artist's first major solo presentation in the city in nearly a decade, the expansive showcase features new 2026 paintings, large-format drawings, recent sculptures and foundational early works from the 1980s chosen by Nara himself.The presentation at the 537 West 20th Street space highlights the latest stylistic shifts in Nara's two-dimensional artwork, featuring front-facing portraits with direct gazes rendered in a distinctly muted, highly nuanced color palette. The new paintings reveal intricate, diffused brushwork that builds richly atmospheric depths, alongside a fresh method where compositions are first sketched in colored pencil before receiving translucent washes of acrylic paint. In these works, figures adopt natural poses with tear-filled eyes that evoke a quiet sense of uncertainty. Exhibited in tandem are recent monochrome drawings created with industrial oil-based paint sticks, as well as his "line" paintings —works created by projecting and reanimating bold notebook sketches onto canvas to retain the rapid, fluid impulse of drawing.Concurrently, the 533 West 19th Street venue houses thirteen monumental bronze head sculptures created in 2024, each representing a ten-fold enlargement of palm-sized clay prototypes hand-molded by the artist. Coated in matte white urethane paint to afford an inviting visual softness, the large-scale works recall the "snow monsters" created by heavy snowfall during Nara's childhood winters. By magnifying the simple facial expressions of these small prototypes to a monumental scale, the installation explores the psychological impact of size, allowing the play of light and shadow across their smooth surfaces to foster an environment of serenity and reflection.Both showcases will take place across its aforementioned gallery locations starting October 29, 2026. items.text: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Fronts Levi's FW26 Campaign and Speaks on His Unfiltered Approach To Style Summary Levi’s has enlisted reigning NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to front its Fall/Winter 2026 Keep it Loose campaignIn an exclusive interview with Hypebeast, Gilgeous-Alexander breaks down his rule-breaking tunnel fits, his Canadian roots, and how he styled the collectionThe NBA superstar builds his campaign looks around foundational denim pieces including the 501 Loose and Baggy Barrel paired with relaxed outerwear Levi's has officially unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 campaign titled "Keep it Loose," placing reigning NBA MVP and style icon Shai Gilgeous-Alexander front and center. Centered around the brand's "Loose Prep" ethos, the campaign challenges rigid dress codes by offering relaxed silhouettes, self-styled proportions, and an effortless approach to traditional wardrobe staples.Given total creative freedom to style himself for the campaign, Gilgeous-Alexander built his outfits around wide-leg denim cuts like the 501® Loose and Baggy Barrel, pairing them with the MA-1 Bomber jacket and Authentic PO Hoodie. Shot on film by director Mel Bles, the campaign centers around capturing the superstar's nonchalant approach to personal style.In an exclusive interview with Hypebeast, Gilgeous-Alexander opened up about his creative process both on and off the court. items.title: Andersson Bell Touches Down in Tokyo With a New Aoyama Flagship
items.text: Andersson Bell Touches Down in Tokyo With a New Aoyama Flagship Summary Andersson Bell opens a new flagship store in Tokyo’s Aoyama district.The interior blends retro-futuristic metal with warm wood and industrial concrete.Launch includes a store‑exclusive T‑shirt and heart‑shaped keyring, alongside a new FW26 campaign shot in Tokyo. Andersson Bell has opened its first Japanese flagship in Tokyo’s Aoyama district. The three‑floor store, co-designed by architecture studio I IN, blends brutalist structure with vibrant color and light to express the brand’s “beauty of contrast.”The flagship occupies a 1993 brutalist building, reimagined with bold color palettes, glossy materials and dynamic lighting to reflect Andersson Bell’s ethos of merging opposites — classic and modern, minimal and expressive. The design narrative emphasizes contrast, with raw concrete surfaces juxtaposed against polished finishes, creating a space that feels both industrial and refined. Spread across a basement and two above‑ground floors, the store functions not only as a retail destination but also as a cultural hub, intended to foster connections with Tokyo’s creative community.To mark the opening, Andersson Bell introduced store‑exclusive items, including a unisex graphic T‑shirt priced at ¥19,800 JPY (approx. $126 USD) and a limited‑edition heart‑shaped leather keyring with a built‑in measuring tape, retailing at ¥9,900 JPY (approx. $63 USD). Both items incorporate the brand’s storytelling motifs, with the T‑shirt featuring poster‑like graphics and the keyring inscribed with the phrase “COINCIDENCE MORE LIKE DESTINY’S PRE‑GAME.” These exclusives highlight Andersson Bell’s commitment to blending fashion with narrative detail, making the flagship a destination for collectors and fans.The opening coincided with the release of Andersson Bell’s FW26 campaign, shot in Tokyo and featuring model SUMIRE under the lens of photographer Kazunori Usui. Creative director Dohun Kim emphasized Tokyo’s long‑standing influence on the brand, positioning the flagship as a new base for cultural exchange and collaboration.ADSB Andersson Bell Aoyama5-49-2 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 150-0001, Japan View this post on Instagram A post shared by ADSB ANDERSSON BELL JP (@adsb_anderssonbell_jp) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: NOT A HOTEL AOSHIMA Expands Its Tropical Japanese Resort With New Luxury Suites
items.text: NOT A HOTEL AOSHIMA Expands Its Tropical Japanese Resort With New Luxury Suites Summary NOT A HOTEL AOSHIMA debuts two new villas, CHILL 2.0 and COAST, designed by Shin Ohori.The CHILL 2.0 maisonette features a 21-meter infinity pool, outdoor lounge, and sauna.The COAST duplex offers a private pool, garden and 3.2-meter ceilings. NOT A HOTEL AOSHIMA has expanded its beachfront retreat in Miyazaki with two new villas, CHILL 2.0 and COAST. The new architecture and room layouts were designed by Shin Ohori of GENERAL DESIGN, who also helmed the original buildings, ensuring a seamless visual harmony with Aoshima's lush, subtropical landscape. By expanding the property's public spaces to include a skateboard park and verdant green park areas, the updated resort invites guests into a richer, more engaging lifestyle experience.Serving as an evolution of the resort's flagship "house of the horizon," the new CHILL 2.0 room is a third-level maisonette designed to maximize panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean. Accommodating up to six guests, this expansive suite features two ocean-view bedrooms that step directly out onto a shared terrace to catch the sea breeze. The focal point of the outdoor space is a massive 21-meter infinity pool, expanded from the original CHILL footprint, which blends effortlessly into the distant horizon. Adjacent to the water, a floating outdoor living area with a sunken sofa and fireplace invites guests to relax, while a seamlessly connected bath, sauna, and cold plunge system ensures a continuous flow of wellness and tranquility.The second new addition, COAST, is a duplex spanning the first and second floors that comfortably accommodates up to four people. Situated on a prime oceanfront plot, this house merges the best elements of the property’s earlier "SURF" and "GARDEN" suites by offering both a private pool and a lush, secluded private garden. One of the four units is pet‑friendly, allowing guests to stay with dogs. Inside, COAST boasts soaring 3.2-meter-high ceilings in the living room, establishing a profound sense of depth and openness that complements the tropical environment.Together, these meticulously crafted residences - alongside the recently renewed, ocean-facing LDK restaurant designed by Ryu Kosaka of A.N.D. - elevate the site’s experience into a fully realized, luxurious beach community. For more details, head over to NOT A HOTEL AOSHIMA’s official website. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Studio Jouin Manku on 20 Years of Shared Creative Ambition With Van Cleef & Arpels
items.text: Studio Jouin Manku on 20 Years of Shared Creative Ambition With Van Cleef & Arpels In a cityscape built on towering skyscrapers and a constant sensory rush, the retail landscape often feels like a loud shouting match to catch people’s attention. Standard luxury storefronts in Hong Kong consistently fight for dominance by making their presence known through grand architectural designs, bold iconography and distinctive branding engineered for instant consumer recognition. Van Cleef & Arpels, however, operates at the opposite extreme.The French High Jewelry Maison embraces a calculated subtlety, frequently tucking its logo away in an unassuming, less in-your-face manner on its store façades to cultivate an intentional sense of mystery that quietly intrigues passersby to look closer inside. It is precisely this quiet philosophy that guides its newly relocated Hong Kong Maison in Central’s Alexandra House. Moving from its home at the Landmark Prince’s Building where it had sat since 2011, Van Cleef & Arpels turned to long-trusted architectural partners Patrick Jouin and Sanjit Manku of Studio Jouin Manku to build something far more complex than a standard storefront: a structural antidote to the modern digital age.The space’s poetic subversion begins with an 825-square-meter stone and textured glass façade that mimics a "rain of light," adorned with giant white plaster petals hand-sculpted by artisans in England. "Can you successfully captivate a modern city by whispering when everyone else is shouting?" Manku muses. "We believed we could, provided the whisper possessed enough depth." This structural whisper continues inside, where a grand winding staircase of oak and light limestone acts as the latest of the studio's ongoing dialogue with the city. By removing sharp corners and rigid lines, the architects guide guests through fluid, homey domestic salons that encourage unhurried exploration. Your partnership with Van Cleef & Arpels began 20 years ago, and you originally designed their first Asian Maison at Landmark Prince's back in 2011. What is it like creatively to return to and rewrite the same Maison footprint in the same city after all these years?Patrick Jouin: We have indeed been working together for a very long time, but every single project presents a completely fresh opportunity. The physical space and the structural flow are always entirely different, meaning we constantly have to discover a new visual language to express the core identity of Van Cl

items.title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Nears $1 Billion Global Debut With Historic $927 Million USD Global Box Office Launch
items.text: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Nears $1 Billion Global Debut With Historic $927 Million USD Global Box Office Launch Summary 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' reached $927 million USD globally in its opening weekend performanceThe international haul delivered $572 million USD across 66 markets led by $121 million USD in ChinaThe film stands behind only 'Avengers: Endgame' for the largest worldwide theatrical opening of all time Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios have officially closed a historic debut weekend with Spider-Man: Brand New Day, grossing $927 million USD worldwide to approach the $1 billion USD threshold in just three days. The record-shattering start ranks as the second-largest global box office opening in cinematic history.Following an unprecedented $72 million USD in Thursday previews and a $168 million USD opening day, the Destin Daniel Cretton-directed feature generated $355 million USD across North America. Overseas markets contributed $572 million USD across 66 international territories, spearheaded by China with $121 million USD, followed by $49 million USD in the United Kingdom and $38.3 million USD in Mexico.The global opening of $927 million USD trails only 2019's Avengers: Endgame ($1.2 billion USD) while comfortably outperforming 2018's Avengers: Infinity War ($640 million USD) and 2021's Spider-Man: No Way Home. Bolstered by a 90% Rotten Tomatoes critics' score and an "A" CinemaScore, the Tom Holland-led installment has established a dominant trajectory as it aims to join the rare $2 billion USD club.Spider-Man: Brand New Day is currently playing in theaters globally. items.text: Carhartt WIP Readies a Texture-Focused FW26 Collection Summary Carhartt WIP drops its FW26 collection, blending archival workwear with modern outdoor cues and fresh washes.Features a hand-finished "destroy wash," "Duck Feather Print," and seasonal colors like Tangled Shady Purple.Priced between $18 – $348 USD, the range is available now via the brand. This Fall/Winter 2026 season, Carhartt WIP continues to blend archival workwear with modern outdoor cues, introducing new fabrics, washes and prints. The new range functions as an exploration of texture, feel and finish, with apparel and accessories reimagining the brand’s quintessential workwear DNA through innovative fabric treatments as well as subtle tailoring influences.Central to the collection is the debut of a hand-finished "destroy wash" technique, which gives heavy canvas silhouettes an aged, heavily weathered quality. Applied to archival staples such as the OG Chore Coat, the Women's OG Arcan Jacket and the OG Double Knee Pant, the abrasive process subtly scuffs seams and hems to ensure each piece arrives pre-aged with unique character.Outerwear pieces such as the Curtis Sweater Jacket and Bolon Sweat Jacket emphasize functionality while incorporating fresh seasonal colors like Tangled Shady Purple and Dark Navy. Denim staples, including the Oakland Shirt Jac and Oakland Pant, arrive in rinsed and worn washes, while knitwear like the 1989 Winners Sweat highlights Carhartt WIP’s balance of durability and style.The collection also introduces new prints and accessories, including the Duck Feather Print seen on the Travon Shirt and Cap, alongside playful graphic T-shirts like the Playing Cards Tee and Cheese Toast Tee. Priced from $18 - $348 USD, the FW26 collection is available globally through Carhartt WIP flagships, select retailers and the brand’s online store. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Marvel Officially Scraps Mahershala Ali-Led ‘Blade’ Reboot After Years of Production Delays
items.text: Marvel Officially Scraps Mahershala Ali-Led ‘Blade’ Reboot After Years of Production Delays Summary 'Blade,' the Mahershala Ali-led film was officially canceled following years of production delays, director departures and creative setbacks.The cancellation leaves production staff unpaid and threatens Arkane Lyon’s standalone 'Blade' video game project amidst studio restructuring. The Mahershala Ali-led Blade movie, first announced in July 2019 fresh off the success of Avengers: Endgame, has been officially scrapped following a series of high-profile setbacks. Ali recently shared diplomatic remarks about moving on from the vampire hunter role and making any future inquiries the studio's problem. While the actor was under contract for years, the ongoing inability to begin production led him to focus on other projects. He now headlines the upcoming October action drama Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, which is notably written and directed by one-time Blade filmmaker Bassam Tariq. Other former cast members have also secured new roles, with Mia Goth on The Odyssey and Aaron Pierre starring in Lanterns.The abrupt cancellation extends beyond the primary cast, leaving stunt actors, costumers and editors without expected paychecks during a turbulent period for the entertainment industry. This ripple effect also threatens the standalone Blade video game announced in 2023 by Dishonored developer Arkane Lyon. Caught in the crossfire of extensive Xbox studio acquisitions and recent mass layoffs, the single-player title is in danger of being permanently shelved. The studio currently relies on a mandatory consultation process granted by French labor laws to stave off immediate closure, leaving the highly anticipated project on life support.Scrapping the high-profile feature adds to a growing wave of industry criticism regarding Marvel's handling of Black-led projects throughout the Multiverse Saga. To fill the supernatural void in its schedule, the studio recently announced a Ghost Rider film starring Ryan Gosling for 2028 alongside the confirmation of a third Black Panther hitting theaters that same year. Fans argue that relying heavily on Wakandan narratives while fumbling a culturally significant character like the Daywalker highlights a major misstep for the franchise.Despite the cinematic drought, the Daywalker continues to exist in other media formats. The character features prominently in recent multiplayer titles like Marvel Rivals and the fighting game Marv

items.title: Form Portfolios Acquires Heritage Label Dansk to Relaunch Midcentury Design Grails
items.text: Form Portfolios Acquires Heritage Label Dansk to Relaunch Midcentury Design Grails Summary Design firm Form Portfolios purchased heritage brand Dansk for $250,000 USD following Food52's Chapter 11 asset auction.Founder Mark Masiello is relocating the design studio to Copenhagen to relaunch archival grails like Kobenstyle cookware. Design licensing firm Form Portfolios has officially taken stewardship of Dansk. The move marks a pivotal return for the beloved Danish-American midcentury design icon after years of corporate transitions. The acquisition by the Rhode Island and Copenhagen-based firm follows a Chapter 11 filing by Food52. The former parent company saw its assets split across multiple bidders during an intense Delaware auction. The heritage tabletop brand served as the final component of the sale and was secured for $250,000.Founded in 1954 by American entrepreneurs Ted and Martha Nierenberg alongside principal designer Jens Quistgaard, the label helped introduce Scandinavian modernism to North American homes. It built a stellar reputation on everyday objects that blended sculptural beauty with high functionality. Form Portfolios founder Mark Masiello had already spent several years working with the Quistgaard family to manage the late creator's archive. Purchasing the company became a deeply personal mission to safeguard a massive design legacy.The forthcoming relaunch strategy aims to restore the original creative formula. After Quistgaard retired, creative control migrated heavily to the United States. Masiello intends to reverse that shift by firmly rooting the design studio back in Copenhagen. The revival will feature a direct-to-consumer channel at Dansk.com. Loyal fans can expect to see reissued archival grails like the iconic Kobenstyle cookware arriving alongside completely new homeware concepts.Addressing a historical blind spot in the product portfolio, the brand is expanding beyond rigid tabletop items. The label utilized the 3 Days of Design 2026 festival in Denmark to announce a major collaboration with 86-year-old textile artist Kim Naver. A defining figure in her field, Naver is currently developing a fresh collection of tabletop textiles. Her involvement signals an early indication of how the revived imprint intends to balance archival continuity with contemporary progression.The resurrection arrives at a crucial moment for the broader interior design market. items.title: Ayaneo Unveils Game Boy Advance-Inspired Konkr Pocket Advance Handheld
items.text: Ayaneo Unveils Game Boy Advance-Inspired Konkr Pocket Advance Handheld Summary Ayaneo's Konkr Pocket Advance revives the classic 2001 Game Boy Advance layout with modern Android emulation tech.It features a 3.5-inch 960x640 LCD screen with 4x point-to-point scaling for authentic retro gaming.Weighing 224 grams, the console packs L2/R2 triggers, USB-C fast charging and classic Navy Blue and Coral Orange colorways. Arriving just after the 25th anniversary of Nintendo’s legendary 2001 hardware, Ayaneo is tapping into peak handheld nostalgia with the Konkr Pocket Advance. Revealed during an official product-sharing stream by CEO Arthur, the new release operates under the brand's dedicated KONKR sub-label. The device strictly maintains the ergonomic horizontal form factor that defined a generation of portable gaming while infusing it with a suite of contemporary hardware upgrades.Front and center is a 3.5-inch LCD screen boasting a 960 x 640 resolution. This specific panel preserves the beloved 3:2 aspect ratio while leveraging 4x point-to-point display technology to deliver crisp integer scaling for classic pixel-art titles. Under the hood, the Android-based system utilizes software emulation rather than vintage cartridges. The hardware operates seamlessly with Ayaneo’s self-developed AYASpace game management ecosystem for streamlined library organization.The physical control layout strikes a balance between retro authenticity and modern utility. It includes a standard D-pad and conductive rubber ABXY buttons alongside oversized L1/R1 bumpers and newly added L2/R2 triggers to handle demanding 3D layouts. A dedicated microSD card slot manages expanded storage, flanked by a USB-C port for PD fast charging, Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0. Preserving the tactile charm of the era, the unit also retains a classic 3.5mm headphone jack and a physical volume adjustment wheel.Measuring slightly thicker than its muse to accommodate the tech, the 224-gram console will debut in two nostalgic finishes: an elegant Navy Blue echoing the original Indigo and a vibrant Coral Orange referencing the classic Spice Orange variant. Pricing and an official release date remain under wraps. Enthusiasts are hoping for a wider production run following the rapid sell-out of the company's recent Pocket Micro 2. For more information, head over to KONKR's official website. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: John Oliver Extends HBO Contract for 'Last Week Tonight' Through 2027 Summary John Oliver has signed a one-year contract extension with HBO to continue hosting 'Last Week Tonight' through 2027The shorter extension represents a shift from the host's customary three-year deal structureThe renewal comes during ongoing uncertainty surrounding Warner Bros Discovery and prospective corporate acquisitions HBO and John Oliver have officially agreed to a contract extension that will keep Last Week Tonight with John Oliver on the network through the end of 2027. The deal extends the Emmy-winning late-night series through its upcoming 14th season.Unlike John Oliver’s previous renewals—which historically secured three-year commitments, including a December 2023 deal that carried the show through Season 13—the current agreement spans a single year. The shorter timeframe comes as parent company Warner Bros. Discovery faces corporate uncertainty surrounding potential acquisition moves, including a proposed deal involving Paramount Skydance.Oliver, who launched the weekly late-night program on HBO in 2014, has frequently addressed the network's shifting corporate ownership on-air. Despite the changing landscape behind the scenes, the extension ensures that Last Week Tonight will maintain its regular broadcast schedule through 2027.Last Week Tonight with John Oliver currently airs new episodes on HBO and streams on Max. items.title: 5 Art-Inspired Films to Put on Your Radar
items.text: 5 Art-Inspired Films to Put on Your Radar A gallerist tries to sell a dead body at Art Basel Miami. Such is the premise of Cathy Yan’s The Gallerist, starring Natalie Portman, Charli xcx, and Jenna Ortega. It premiered at January’s Sundance Film Festival, and while it’s yet to land a wider release, the film, and its gloriously absurd premise, seemed to set off a chain across the theaters and festival circuit: a sudden appetite for art world mystique.Cinephiles are particularly well-fed this season. Between Obsession and Backrooms, horror is having another scorching summer, but so too is contemporary art. Before the Venice Film Festival opens the gates for September’s stacked calendar — from Frieze London and Seoul to The Armory Show in New York — consider these releases your fall warm-up.I Want Your Sex dir. Gregg ArakiSex, crime, and art are the big three in Gregg Araki’s silver-screen homecoming, I Want Your Sex, which premiered at the top of 2026 at the Sundance Film Festival. Olivia Wilde plays Erika Tracy, an art star and provocateur, opposite Cooper Hoffman as Elliot, her apathetic Gen Z assistant, alongside more than several notable names, like Charli, Chase Sui Wonders, Daveed Diggs, and Margaret Cho. The film is now showing in U.S. theaters nationwide.Joie de Vivre dir. Luca GuadagninoClocking in at seven hours, Joie de Vivre is Luca Guadagnino’s odyssey of a documentary dedicated to the legendary Italian artist and filmmaker, Bernardo Bertolucci. This is Guadagnino’s second cinematic project surrounding his artistic mentor after Bertolucci on Bertolucci (2013), which he dubs his “most personal” film, and is set to premiere Out of Competition at the upcoming Venice Film Festival later this month.Barrio Triste dir. StillzBarrio Triste isn’t about the art world, per se, but with Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz as director, EDGLRD on production, and a soundtrack by Arca, the stacked team makes it a natural next-up on our list. The found-footage work, which premiered at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, follows four teenagers in a hauntingly tender portrait of late '80s Medellín, Colombia. The film is currently showing in select theaters across the U.S.Avedon dir. Ron HowardAfter a standout Cannes premiere, Ron Howard’s Richard Avedon documentary is coming to Netflix later this year. The film traces Avedon’s life and legacy, “whose work continues to resonate not only because of the extraordinary images he created, but because of the humanity and curiosity

items.title: CMF Debuts the Ultra-Lightweight Clip Pro Open-Ear Earbuds
items.text: CMF Debuts the Ultra-Lightweight Clip Pro Open-Ear Earbuds CMF has officially expanded its audio lineup with the new CMF Clip Pro, marking the brand’s first foray into the open-ear earbud market. Designed for users navigating busy cities and active lifestyles, the earbuds prioritize a natural listening experience that maintains environmental awareness without sacrificing comfort or sound quality.Engineered around a proprietary 3-point Clip Design, the earbuds feature a slim C-bridge with an elastic titanium wire core that flexes to fit any ear shape, distributing pressure evenly rather than concentrating it in one spot. Weighing just 6.5 grams each, the Clip Pro utilizes skin-friendly materials and an optimized listening ball to ensure long-term comfort while efficiently directing sound toward the ear canal.Despite its lightweight, open-ear construction, the Clip Pro is built to deliver premium wireless audio. The earbuds are equipped with a custom-tuned 10.8 mm dual-magnet dynamic driver and utilize CMF's Ultra Bass Technology to intelligently enhance low frequencies and reduce treble distortion, compensating for the natural bass loss typical of open-ear designs. The devices are also Hi-Res Audio Certified and support high-quality streaming codecs including LDAC, AAC and SBC. To ensure clear communication in noisy environments, the Clip Pro integrates a VPU-powered Clear Voice Technology and a 4 HD microphone system, alongside a customizable Sound Seal system designed to reduce audio leakage and protect user privacy during calls and playback.Aligning with CMF’s distinctive, playful industrial design language, the Clip Pro is available in three distinct colorways: Dark Grey, Light Grey and Coral. A standout feature is the signature Smart Dial integrated directly into the charging case, allowing users to quickly adjust volume, manage playback, and handle calls without needing to interact with their phones. Built to withstand daily wear, the IP54-rated earbuds offer up to 10 hours of continuous playback—extending to 32.5 hours with the case—and support fast charging, Bluetooth 5.4, and Dual Device Connection. The CMF Clip Pro is available starting today on the brand's official webstore, retailing for $99 USD. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Hikari no Yami Questions Identity and Form in SS27 “Chapter 11: Parasite”
items.text: Hikari no Yami Questions Identity and Form in SS27 “Chapter 11: Parasite” Summary Hikari no Yami's SS27 collection interrogates identity via the Ship of Theseus paradox.Collection features recycled fabrics, resin-encapsulated tops, and Alpha Industries collaborations.Campaign highlights hand-painted shirts, molded spines, and sculptural aesthetics shot in Paris. Hikari no Yami has unveiled its Spring/Summer 2027 collection, titled "Chapter 11: Parasite," marking a pivotal evolution for the brand after ten seasons of deconstructing tailoring and philosophical concepts. Positioned between the opposing tenets of absurdism and essentialism, the collection engages with the "Ship of Theseus" paradox to question whether identity is inherently fixed or continuously rebuilt. To explore this concept, the brand dismantled and reconstructed reused fabrics - including recycled cotton, wool and Japanese nylon mesh - using hand-stitching, painting, dyeing, spraying and resin encapsulation to expose internal garment architecture and form entirely new expressions.Key collaborations enrich the collection: Alpha Industries lends military utility silhouettes reassembled into expressions of individuality, while designer Ciera Calmeise contributes molded spines and resin tops. Artist Vanessa Vun hand-paints ink-dyed dress shirts, and Alex Yarally introduces Japanese nylon mesh tops, Supima shirting dusters, and silk chiffon hoodies. These pieces highlight the brand’s philosophy of garments as mutable, never fixed and always evolving. Captured by photographer Roman Pushkarskii, the accompanying campaign visually anchors the collection’s raw, sculptural aesthetics in stark outdoor settings. items.title: AI Demand Triggers Severe Global Stock Shortages for the Apple MacBook Air
items.text: AI Demand Triggers Severe Global Stock Shortages for the Apple MacBook Air Summary The global memory chip shortage fueled by intense demand from AI companies has begun impacting the availability of the MacBook AirShipping estimates on Apple's online store for many configurations have slipped into late August and SeptemberApple has attempted to mitigate the shortage by raising prices for Mac models and sourcing components from Chinese suppliers The global memory chip shortage has officially come for Apple’s most popular computer. While the industry-wide supply squeeze initially impacted niche machines like the Mac mini and Mac Studio, the crunch is now causing widespread availability issues for the MacBook Air. The component deficit, driven by the insatiable demands of AI companies, has fundamentally disrupted retail operations and created what Apple CEO Tim Cook described as a "hundred-year flood" for the tech supply chain.Consumers looking to purchase a new laptop are facing significant hurdles. Shipments for various configurations on Apple's official store have already slipped into the latter half of August, with some custom setups delayed until September. At the retail level, physical Apple locations are experiencing unprecedented inventory constraints. Shoppers are finding shelves completely bare in multiple regions. The shortage underscores a broader market reality where memory manufacturers are prioritizing high-paying AI clients over traditional consumer electronics.To navigate the volatile supply and demand imbalance, Apple has been forced to recalibrate its pricing and marketing strategies. The tech giant recently implemented a $200 USD price hike for the M5 MacBook Air to offset surging component costs. Simultaneously, the company delayed its highly anticipated annual back-to-school promotion and heavily shifted its marketing focus toward the base model 14-inch MacBook Pro. For the first time, promotional materials for the ultraportable laptop now carry a distinct "subject to availability" warning.Behind the scenes, executives are aggressively seeking alternative solutions to keep the MacBook Air in production. The brand is actively lobbying for regulatory approval to source components from Chinese memory suppliers like CXMT to stabilize inventory for domestic markets. Until the global pipeline recovers from the AI boom, securing Apple’s flagship everyday machine will require significant patience and a slightly heavier wallet. Click here to view

items.title: Panerai Outfits the Luminor Marina PAM01707 in High-Tech Carbotech™
items.text: Panerai Outfits the Luminor Marina PAM01707 in High-Tech Carbotech™ Summary Panerai drops the 44mm Luminor Marina PAM01707 in lightweight Carbotech™.The matte black sandwich dial features vintage beige Super-LumiNova® and omits the date.Powered by the P.9010 caliber, it offers 300-meter water resistance. Panerai has officially introduced the new Luminor Marina PAM01707, a timepiece that blends the Maison's 1960s naval design codes with advanced high-tech material innovation. Framed in a bold 44mm case, the watch is constructed from Carbotech™, a carbon fiber composite compressed with PEEK (Polyether Ether Ketone) polymer under high pressure and temperature. This proprietary material yields a matte black, unevenly textured surface that ensures every individual piece has a unique appearance. Remarkably light yet exceptionally tough, Carbotech™ is 64% lighter than titanium and 80% lighter than steel, offering superior strength-to-weight performance and extreme corrosion resistance suited for marine exploration.At the heart of the PAM01707 is a matte black sandwich dial adorned with warm beige Super-LumiNova® that glows green in the dark, delivering a distinctly vintage tool-watch aesthetic. In a nod to Panerai's historical commissions for the Royal Italian Navy, the date window has been omitted to maintain a clean, distraction-free layout. The dial retains a small seconds sub-dial at 9 o'clock — a feature originally designed for Italian commandos to verify that the watch was running under extreme operational conditions. The 14.5mm thick case features a DLC-coated titanium closed caseback and is paired with a warm brown vintage calf leather strap with beige stitching, alongside a second black rubber strap for sportier, aquatic pursuits.Powering the watch is the in-house P.9010 automatic caliber, a 6mm-thick movement built from 200 components and 31 jewels. Operating at 28,800 alternations per hour (4 Hz), its two series-connected barrels deliver a robust three-day power reserve. The movement integrates practical real-world functions, including a stop-seconds feature for precise synchronization and a quick time-change mechanism that allows the hour hand to jump forward or backward in one-hour increments without disrupting the minute hand. Tested to an impressive water resistance of 30 bar (~300 meters) with an additional 25% safety margin, the Luminor Marina PAM01707 is available via Panerai's official website and physical boutiques. Responsible for nearly a quarter of Maranello’s global footprint, the United States now serves as the canvas for the Purosangue American Grand Tour Atelier Collection. Built as ten completely unique, one-of-one commissions, these bespoke V12 crossovers pull direct inspiration from the country's sweeping landscapes and historic driving routes, ensuring no two vehicles in the lineup will ever be duplicated.The collection opens with the Landscapes series, a five-car study translating regional topographies into rich visual contrasts. "The Coast" sets the tone by pairing Blu Cangiante paint with Dark Amber accents and Terra Antica leather, capturing the meeting point of Pacific waves and coastal bluffs. "Switchback" merges Blu America paint with a sharp Rosso Corsa livery, anchoring an interior lined in Bianco white leather with stars-and-stripes detailing stitched directly into the seats. "Overlook" flips that palette with Rosso California paint, a Blu America livery, and a clean Bianco interior. "Straight Away" rocks a Bianco Mille Miglia finish with classic blue NART racing stripes over rich Rosso Giudecca leather, which is then inverted by "Byway" in a Blu NART body with a Bianco King livery. items.title: Mercedes-Benz to Bring Back Physical Cabin Controls Across Future Models
items.text: Mercedes-Benz to Bring Back Physical Cabin Controls Across Future Models Summary CEO Ola Källenius admitted the brand prioritized technology over convenience and will reintroduce tactile switches to future cabins.Expansive displays like the 56-inch MBUX Hyperscreen will remain central, working alongside restored physical controls.The shift addresses user distraction concerns and upcoming 2026 Euro NCAP regulations requiring physical switches for safety functions Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Källenius acknowledged that the company prioritized technology over customer convenience by eliminating physical controls across its modern lineup. Speaking in an interview with Autocar, Källenius noted that the global automotive industry reached a "low button" point and suggested future cabin designs will aim for a harmonious balance between digital real estate and tactile feedback. The executive joked that a vehicle interface needs to be simple enough for either a five-year-old or a board member to operate seamlessly.The reversal follows years of interior development centered around massive glass interfaces. Despite the restoration of some physical switches, Mercedes-Benz does not intend to reduce the overall size or number of screens in upcoming models such as the 2027 Mercedes GLA. Displays like the expansive 56-inch MBUX Hyperscreen will continue to dominate the cabin architecture. The luxury brand plans to let giant touchscreens and traditional switches coexist rather than allowing one to entirely replace the other.This interior design adjustment aligns with recent pivots from other luxury vehicle manufacturers responding to consumer preferences for intuitive controls. Competitor brands including Ferrari, Volkswagen and Hyundai have also started reversing the all-touch philosophy to improve daily drivability. The industry shift is not purely driven by user complaints. Upcoming Euro NCAP regulations slated for 2026 will penalize automakers that fail to provide physical switches for essential functions like turn signals, hazard lights and windshield wipers.Competitive testing and safety studies have consistently highlighted the ergonomic benefits of physical buttons for high-frequency tasks behind the wheel. A recent Swedish distraction test demonstrated that drivers operating a button-heavy vehicle completed everyday cabin tasks significantly faster than those navigating menus in touchscreen-focused models. items.title: Tim Cook Hints Heavy Apple Intelligence Users Will Soon Have to Pay
items.text: Tim Cook Hints Heavy Apple Intelligence Users Will Soon Have to Pay Summary Tim Cook confirmed Apple Intelligence will not remain entirely free, signaling paid add-ons for heavy users.Server-side processing costs will drive a freemium model where power users can "buy up the stack."The revamped Siri AI is currently in iOS 27 public beta ahead of its official fall rollout. During Apple's Q3 2026 earnings call on July 30, 2026, outgoing CEO Tim Cook delivered a reality check for users anticipating unlimited access to the highly anticipated Siri AI. Cook signaled that heavy reliance on the new generative tools will likely come with a price tag. The comments mark the first official acknowledgment that Apple Intelligence features will not remain entirely free for high-volume users.Apple reported a massive $109.4 billion USD in revenue for the June quarter. Amid the financial breakdown, Goldman Sachs questioned how the tech giant plans to offset the massive computing costs associated with server-side AI processing. Cook kept the exact pricing structure vague but confirmed that heavy users will need to open their wallets. He noted that the company anticipates a dedicated segment of users who will push the limits of the system.To accommodate this demand, Cook stated that the brand will introduce upgrade possibilities on iCloud+ where consumers can buy up the stack. This phrasing indicates a shift from simply requiring a base cloud subscription. Power users might need to pay an additional premium strictly for extended server access.The underlying cost stems from how the new features operate. Apple designed its tools to process as much data on-device as possible to protect user privacy and minimize server overhead. Complex tasks still require offloading to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers and partner networks like Google Gemini. Running massive language models in the cloud requires significant infrastructure investment. A freemium model mirrors the strategy already utilized by other major chatbot developers.The revamped digital assistant is currently available to testers in the iOS 27 public beta. The update brings a conversational interface and the ability to take action across multiple apps. With the general release slated for September, users have a limited window before Apple defines exactly where the free tier ends and the paid subscription begins. items.title: Lamborghini Reports Record €1.74 Billion EUR Revenue for H1 2026
items.text: Lamborghini Reports Record €1.74 Billion EUR Revenue for H1 2026 Summary Lamborghini’s H1 2026 revenue grew 7.4% to €1.74 billion EUR, with operating profit hitting €395 million EUR despite a 4.6% delivery dipHigh-margin custom options, resilient pricing and tight supply control successfully offset geopolitical tensions, Chinese luxury downturns and US import tariffs. Lamborghini reported a seemingly paradoxical financial performance for the first half of 2026. The Italian automaker generated €1.74 billion EUR in revenue between January and June. This figure represents a 7.4 percent increase compared to the same period last year. Total operating profit reached €395 million EUR. Deliveries actually declined by 4.6% during this six-month window. The brand handed over 5,422 vehicles to customers globally.Several external market factors constrained overall sales volume. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and a noticeable downturn in the Chinese luxury sector dampened demand in those specific regions. Increased US import tariffs introduced in 2025 further complicated the international delivery landscape. Growing economic uncertainty across the European market also played a role in the slight dip in shipped units.Company executives attribute the revenue growth to a resilient pricing strategy and an unwavering focus on exclusivity. Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer Paolo Poma noted that adverse exchange rates and tariff penalties did not compromise the underlying strength of the Lamborghini brand. By maintaining a tight grip on supply and prioritizing high-margin custom configurations, the automaker successfully offset the lower physical output with higher per-unit profitability.The product pipeline remains highly active as Lamborghini navigates these global headwinds. Customer deliveries for the new Temerario started in the first quarter. This rollout fully integrates the highly anticipated Huracan successor into the broader lineup. The automaker also expanded its electrified portfolio at the start of July with the introduction of the flagship Urus SE Performante. The plug-in hybrid super SUV utilizes a twin-turbocharged V8 paired with an electric motor to produce a combined 801 horsepower.Demand for existing models continues to outpace production capacity.
